chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Ibn al-Mughira from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who freed a slave and then died. He said, 'The right of manumission (walayah) returns to the sons of her father.'

key_terms.بَنِي أَبِيهَا: The sons of her father (paternal brothers)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the right of manumission (walayah) when a woman frees a slave and dies?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the right of manumission (walayah) for a slave freed by a woman reverts to her paternal lineage (bani abiha) upon her death, distinguishing it from general inheritance rules. This ruling highlights the specific juristic principle in Shia fiqh that walayah follows the paternal line for both men and women, ensuring the freed slave remains within the father's family unit rather than dispersing to the maternal side or other heirs.
